title: Trains to Kemble
lead: These are the trains I would look at if you’d like to use the free South Cerney Fast Track Park and Ride for the Royal International Air Tattoo. Kemble is the closest station to RAF Fairford, but there’s no shuttle from it, so it’s a short taxi to South Cerney, where taxis can drop you off, and then the free Fast Track bus to the Yellow entry. Pick your station, a day and a time below.
facts: Every day, buses Friday to Sunday
Taxi to South Cerney, about 15 minutes
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the South Cerney Fast Track. Book your taxi from here before the day. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
ysh3b: Fast Track bus and taxi back
walkLine: Kemble is a small station, so I would book a taxi from here to the South Cerney Fast Track before the day. I’ve listed some local firms further down the page. It’s about 8 miles and 15 minutes, and taxis are allowed to drop you off there. Security and ticket checks are done at South Cerney, then the free bus takes you along its own route to the Yellow entry.
walkBack: The Fast Track buses back leave from the Yellow entry. I would agree a pick up time at South Cerney with your taxi before you go, as phone signal on the showground can be poor.
offTag: Taxi from here to South Cerney
note: Train times are from the National Rail timetable for Thursday 5 to Sunday 8 November 2026 (Monday to Wednesday use the Thursday times), checked on 30 October 2026, so they are a guide to how trains run on those days of the week rather than the show weekend times. The Fast Track bus hours are the latest ones published for RIAT, and the bus journey time is my estimate and may change for 2027. Times for summer 2027 usually come out in the spring, so please check before you travel. The railway and the bus route are drawn along the lines and roads, so treat them as a guide. gaOnly: Trains to Kemble, a taxi, then the free Fast Track bus. GWR runs the trains through Kemble, roughly hourly between London, Swindon and Gloucester or Cheltenham. I’ve only included the big stations where the trip works.

bus.offDay: check what’s on at RAF Fairford before you travel, as the Fast Track is only laid on for the show days

bus.getThereLong: Take your taxi to South Cerney and go through the checks. With buses leaving all the time, you should be on one by about
bus.thereHead: Buses run all day, shown here every 15 minutes
bus.queue: Around 100 double decker buses run from South Cerney, so you shouldn’t wait long, but security and ticket checks happen before you get on.
bus.queueBack: Leave plenty of time to cross the showground to the Yellow entry, and give your taxi a realistic pick up time.
bus.tip: The South Cerney Fast Track is free. Taxis can drop off and pick up there, so I would book one from Kemble both ways before the day, as local firms get very busy on show weekend.
notes: The Fast Track Park and Ride is free for everyone. Taxis and lifts can drop off and pick up at South Cerney, which you can’t do at the showground itself.
Security and ticket checks happen at South Cerney, so have your RIAT ticket ready before you get on the bus.
The bus hours shown are the latest RIAT has put out, from 07:00 to 18:15 on the Friday and 06:15 to 19:45 at the weekend. The 20 minute ride is my estimate.
Kemble station is small, with roughly one train an hour, so I would check your train home before you leave the showground.
